hero.headline: Nine workers confirmed dead in Longview paper mill disaster
hero.body:
Nine employees have been confirmed dead following a chemical tank rupture at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging facility in Longview, Washington. Recovery crews have retrieved the remains of six victims, with two workers still unaccounted for.

The disaster occurred on Tuesday morning when an industrial tank ruptured and released white liquor, a highly caustic chemical solution used in paper manufacturing. The tank held approximately 600,000 gallons of the liquid, which is primarily made of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide. White liquor is used with heat to break down wood into kraft paper, a durable material used in packaging and other products.

The initial death toll was one confirmed fatality, with nine people injured. One hospitalized worker later died from injuries sustained in the incident. Seven workers remain hospitalized, along with a firefighter who responded to the scene.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson described the incident as potentially "the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." Recovery operations began Wednesday after initial delays due to safety concerns about the structural integrity of the damaged tank. Officials indicated there was no hope of finding additional survivors and shifted operations from rescue to recovery efforts.

The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board launched an investigation into the tank rupture. The cause of the failure remained unknown as of Wednesday.

Among the missing workers were two brothers who worked at the facility together, according to reports. The sprawling Longview plant employs about 1,000 people and produces material for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons.

After the rupture, white liquor spilled into a drainage ditch and contaminated the Columbia River. Dead carp were found following the spill, and authorities urged the public to avoid ditches and dikes while the area undergoes water testing. Officials said there were no issues with air quality or drinking water in Longview.

The tank still contained approximately 25,000 gallons of white liquor, which slowly leaked following the rupture. The Washington state department of ecology and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency are overseeing operations to determine environmental impacts.

The Nippon facility had faced safety complaints in March and May. According to Washington's labor and industries department, those complaints were unrelated to the tank that ruptured. One complaint involved a different valve. Since 2021, Nippon Dynawave has been fined $3,400 for three separate health and safety violations.

Brian Wood with Nippon Dynawave stated that the company was "focused on the victims and helping first responders recover the missing." He said the company would "cooperate to the maximum extent" with the investigation.

cards.headline: Trump postpones decision on Iran ceasefire proposal
cards.teaser: The president delayed a final determination on a tentative US-Iran agreement after meeting with advisers.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers in a Situation Room meeting to make a final determination on a proposed Iran ceasefire agreement. Officials have confirmed that the US and Iran have agreed on a framework for a deal, though Trump did not announce a decision following the meeting.

The tentative ceasefire agreement now awaits the president's approval before it can be implemented. Vice President Vance indicated that the US and Iran have made progress in negotiations.

cards.headline: Oil Posts Biggest Monthly Drop Since 2020
cards.teaser: Oil prices suffered their steepest monthly decline in six years as markets reacted to potential changes in Middle East supply.
cards.body:
Brent crude futures declined 19% since the end of April, marking the steepest monthly fall since 2020. Investors drove down prices as hopes grew for a US-Iran peace deal that could influence regional stability and oil supply.

Stock markets rallied despite the oil pullback, with the Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq reaching new closing highs. Technology stocks led the advance, with the S&P 500 extending its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks.

cards.headline: SEC Proposes Repeal of Climate Disclosure Rule
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a regulation requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed repealing a rule requiring publicly traded companies to disclose their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks. The regulation was finalized during the Biden administration and mandated detailed climate data in corporate financial filings.

The move represents a significant policy reversal under the Trump administration's SEC leadership, which has prioritized rolling back environmental reporting standards established by the previous administration.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: SpaceX secured major government contracts ahead of its initial public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX has secured $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, as disclosed in the company's IPO filing. The awards underscore the military's substantial investment in the company's capabilities for national security space operations.

Government contracts represent a major revenue driver for SpaceX, accounting for one-fifth of the company's 2025 revenue. The significant reliance on defense work highlights SpaceX's dual role as both a commercial space operator and a critical defense contractor as it prepares for its public offering.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test at Cape Canaveral
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Launch Complex 36 in Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night at 9pm ET. The massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launchpad seconds after the start of the scheduled test. The explosion was visible across Florida's space coast, with an orange sky reported in Fort Pierce, about 115 miles to the south. Shockwaves from the blast were felt by residents in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach, and people hundreds of miles away in South Carolina reported seeing a glow in the sky.

Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin's founder, confirmed on social media that all employees were accounted for and safe. He called it "a very rough day" but said the company would investigate the cause and rebuild whatever needed rebuilding. Blue Origin described the incident as "an anomaly" and did not immediately disclose the root cause. Flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the explosion. Emergency officials reported there was no threat from fumes or other hazards.

The explosion comes just days after NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intended to use for these missions, including launching landers that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface. The incident threatens NASA's timeline for building the lunar base and returning humans to the moon within the next two years.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline following the explosion. He noted that spaceflight is unforgiving and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult. NASA stated it would work with partners to support a thorough investigation and assess impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs.

This setback adds to Blue Origin's recent challenges as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts related to the Artemis program. Last month, a payload from the third flight of New Glenn ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

Blue Origin and SpaceX have both built large facilities at Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions with NASA. Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander is scheduled to be tested during the Artemis III mission in 2027, competing against SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which will carry astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface during Artemis IV in 2028.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from case accusing former FBI Director Comey of threatening Trump
cards.teaser: The lead federal prosecutor stepped aside from the seashells photo case without providing an explanation.
cards.body:
The lead prosecutor on the case against former FBI Director James Comey has withdrawn without explanation. Comey faces charges related to posting a photo of seashells arranged to read '86 47,' which prosecutors alleged was a threat against Trump.

The trial has been postponed to October. The Department of Justice has not explained why the lead prosecutor left the case or who will replace them in pursuing charges against the former FBI director.

hero.headline: Russian drone hits Romanian apartment building near Ukraine border
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in the Romanian city of Galati on Friday, injuring two people in what officials said was the first such incident to cause civilian casualties in the NATO member country. The strike occurred during a Russian overnight attack on neighboring Ukraine, with the drone crossing into Romanian airspace before crashing into the residential building.

The impact sparked a fire and forced the evacuation of several residents. Romanian military scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter authorized to engage targets in response to the incident.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte responded swiftly to the strike. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte said after speaking with Romanian President Nicusor Dan. "I affirm that NATO stands ready to defend every inch of allied territory."

Romanian officials confirmed the drone was tracked by radar in the country's airspace before impact. The government said it would officially communicate consequences for diplomatic relations with Russia and indicated it could invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions within the alliance about threats to a member's security.

Romania's foreign minister, Oana Toiu, described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and serious breach of international law. The government asked NATO to accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and said it would prepare measures regarding its relationship with Moscow.

President Dan stated that Romania would not accept the war being transferred to its citizens and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare a proportionate response package.

Russian President Vladimir Putin denied responsibility for the incident, suggesting without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon. He said he had only just learned of the strike and called for the drone wreckage to be handed over to Russia for an independent investigation.

NATO and European Union officials swiftly condemned the incident. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line" and expressed full solidarity with Romania.

Ukraine's foreign minister noted the incident demonstrated that Russian aggression poses a threat to all of Europe and the Black Sea region. France's foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot also condemned what he called Russia's irresponsible act.

The strike represents the latest example of the Ukraine war spilling across borders. Romanian military commanders noted that while the incident was not a direct attack from Russia against Romania, it demonstrated that Russia represents a security threat to countries in the region.

The incident comes as Russia has intensified systematic strikes against Ukraine, employing long-range ballistic missiles and drones to damage infrastructure and cities.

cards.headline: Ghana parliament passes law criminalizing same-sex acts and LGBTQ identification
cards.teaser: Lawmakers approved a bill that makes identifying as gay, lesbian, or transgender punishable by jail time.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that criminalizes same-sex acts and penalizes individuals who identify as gay, lesbian, or transgender with jail time. The bill also targets the promotion of LGBTQ activities.

The measure now requires the president's signature to become law. The parliamentary vote came after lawmakers debated the bill's provisions aimed at the LGBTQ community.

cards.headline: Canadian man pleads guilty to aiding 14 suicides by selling toxic chemicals online
cards.teaser: A man admitted to sending suicide packets containing lethal substances to hundreds of people worldwide.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law appeared in an Ontario courtroom and pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide. He had sold lethal chemicals online with instructions to people across multiple countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia, and New Zealand. Prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges in exchange for the guilty plea.

Law mailed "suicide packets" to more than 100 people worldwide. Families of victims have called for additional charges, particularly in the UK where 79 deaths are linked to his actions. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran cease-fire proposal after meeting with advisers
cards.teaser: The president met with aides for two hours about a possible cease-fire extension after earlier suggesting he was ready to decide.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump postponed his decision on an Iran cease-fire proposal following a two-hour meeting with advisers at the White House. A senior administration official confirmed the discussions centered on a possible cease-fire extension.

The delay came after Trump had signaled on social media that he was ready to make a determination. US and Iranian officials had previously announced they reached agreement on a deal framework, though no agreement was announced after the meeting.

cards.headline: European Union to release 16 billion euros to Hungary after Orban's electoral defeat
cards.teaser: The funds had been withheld as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption and rule of law policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release €16.4 billion to Hungary that was previously frozen under Viktor Orbán's rule. The decision follows the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who has described it as a "historic breakthrough." EU Commission President Ursula von der Lejeunesse hailed the "winds of change" in the country since Magyar took office less than three weeks ago.

The funds had been withheld due to governance and rule of law concerns. The policy shift is already evident: Hungarian police announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest, reversing the previous government's attempt to block the event last year.

cards.headline: Iranian hard-liners rally against potential deal with United States
cards.teaser: A small but vocal faction has used state media and public statements to try to undermine negotiations.
cards.body:
A political fight is unfolding in Iran as hard-liners attempt to derail a potential deal with the United States. The small but loud faction has organized rallies and used state media, along with private and public statements, to try to undermine negotiations.

The effort comes as US and Iranian officials work toward an agreement. The hard-line opposition has mounted a coordinated campaign to block any potential settlement between Tehran and Washington.

cards.headline: Trump's boat strikes fail to reduce cocaine flow to United States, experts say
cards.teaser: Despite a rising body count off the South American coast, cocaine remains widely available.
cards.body:
President Trump's military strikes against drug-smuggling boats off South America have not curbed the flow of cocaine into the United States, researchers say. Despite the rising number of casualties from the operations, experts report cocaine is as easy to obtain in many parts of the country as before the strikes began.

The strikes have targeted vessels off the South American coast used to transport narcotics. The increased enforcement has led to deaths but has not reduced drug availability in US markets, according to the assessment.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Bondi tells lawmakers she was not responsible for Epstein files release
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi placed responsibility on Todd Blanche and Kash Patel when pressed about redaction errors in Jeffrey Epstein documents.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before lawmakers about errors in the release of Jeffrey Epstein files, distancing herself from responsibility for the redaction mistakes. She deflected questions to others involved in the document release process.

The testimony, which occurred about a month after Bondi was ousted by President Donald Trump, has now focused Democratic scrutiny on Todd Blanche and his role in handling the files. Bondi also declined to answer questions about Trump's involvement in the Epstein probe.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from case accusing former FBI Director Comey of threatening Trump
cards.teaser: The lead federal prosecutor stepped aside from the seashells photo case without providing an explanation.

The trial has been postponed to October. The Department of Justice has not explained why the lead prosecutor left the case or who will replace them in pursuing charges against the former FBI director.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge blocked the Kennedy Center closure and name change, prompting Trump to say he will transfer the venue to Congress.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center memorial. The court also blocked plans to close the performing arts center for a two-year renovation, ruling that the Washington cultural institution must remain open.

Following the judicial decision, Trump stated he has no interest in the Kennedy Center and indicated he would transfer it to Congress. The president's response came after the court rejected his efforts to rename the memorial.

cards.headline: Customs official considers pulling officers from Newark airport
cards.teaser: The plan to punish sanctuary jurisdictions by restricting international flights has drawn warnings from airlines and business groups.
cards.body:
Acting Customs and Border Protection official Mullin is weighing whether to pull customs officers from Newark airport as part of a plan to pressure sanctuary jurisdictions. Airlines and business groups have warned the move would create chaos for international travel.

The proposal to restrict international flights at certain airports has faced opposition from the airline industry and lawmakers. Questions remain about how federal immigration enforcement would operate at major events, including the World Cup, if the plan moves forward.

cards.headline: Trump postpones call with Taiwan's president
cards.teaser: The scheduled conversation was put on hold amid tensions over US arms sales to Taiwan.
cards.body:
President Trump has postponed a planned call with Taiwan's president amid ongoing tensions over US military support for the island. A proposed arms package focused on air defense systems has been delayed.

The postponement reflects broader diplomatic friction between Washington and Beijing. China has been pressing Trump to reduce weapons sales to Taiwan, viewing them as interference in its internal affairs. US arms sales to Taiwan follow a formal process that has become a recurring point of contention in US-China relations.

cards.headline: Universal Music Rejects Bill Ackman's $65 Billion Takeover Offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, calling the bid inadequate.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group rejected a $64 billion to $65 billion takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's Pershing Square investment firm, stating the offer fundamentally and materially undervalued the business.

Pershing Square already holds a stake in Universal Music Group. The rejection marks a significant blow to Ackman's attempt to acquire one of the world's largest music companies, which manages recordings and publishing rights for many major artists.

cards.headline: Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Moringa Supplements Sold at Major Retailers
cards.teaser: Health officials linked a salmonella outbreak affecting residents in Washington state to moringa supplement capsules sold through Amazon, Walmart, and Target.
cards.body:
Residents across eastern and western Washington contracted salmonella infections traced to moringa supplement capsules. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention identified the supplements as the outbreak source, leading to a widespread recall.

The contaminated products were distributed through Amazon, Walmart, Target, and TikTok Shop. The Food and Drug Administration announced the recall as illnesses spread across multiple states. Consumers who purchased the affected moringa capsules were instructed to discontinue use immediately.

cards.headline: Wall Street Anticipates SpaceX Public Offering
cards.teaser: Elon Musk and investment bankers are working to build investor demand for a major SpaceX public offering.
cards.body:
Elon Musk is collaborating with bankers to prepare for a massive public offering of SpaceX. The strategy aims to create investor enthusiasm by emphasizing the risks of missing out on the offering rather than the risks of investing in the company.

The approach reflects Wall Street's concern about being excluded from what could be one of the largest initial public offerings in recent years. Investment firms are positioning themselves to participate in the deal as Musk and his financial advisors work to structure the offering.

cards.headline: Train Fire at Penn Station Injures Five, Disrupts Service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train fire near Penn Station injured five people and caused widespread disruptions to rail service during evening rush hour.
cards.body:
A fire broke out on an Amtrak maintenance train near Penn Station during evening rush hour, injuring five people. The blaze forced Amtrak to halt service through the tunnels serving the transit hub, causing significant disruptions for commuters on NJ Transit and the Long Island Rail Road.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority identified tunnel maintenance as an ongoing challenge at the major transit facility, with fires and maintenance issues creating repeated service interruptions for commuter rail lines.

hero.headline: Federal government proposes rule changes allowing grant cancellations at any time
hero.body:
The US government has proposed new funding rules that would allow officials to cancel research grants at any time, according to reports. The changes would also make peer review optional for grant applications.

Under the proposed rules, political staff would screen grant applications for forbidden topics before approval. The changes represent a significant shift in how federal research funding operates, moving away from traditional peer review processes that have guided scientific grant awards.

The proposal affects how billions of dollars in federal research funding would be distributed across universities, research institutions, and individual scientists. Grant recipients currently operate under agreements that provide funding stability for approved project durations.

Peer review has served as the standard method for evaluating scientific merit in federal grant competitions. The process involves independent experts assessing proposals based on scientific quality, methodology, and potential impact. Making this step optional removes a key safeguard in the grant approval process.

The addition of political staff screening introduces a new layer of review focused on identifying forbidden topics. This screening would occur before scientific merit evaluation, changing the order in which grant applications are assessed.

Researchers typically rely on multi-year grants to conduct experiments, hire staff, and publish findings. The ability to cancel grants at any time introduces uncertainty into long-term research planning. Scientists working on active grants could see their funding terminated without the protections currently built into grant agreements.

Federal agencies including the National Institutes of Health and National Science Foundation distribute research funding through competitive grant programs. These agencies have historically used peer review to maintain scientific standards and ensure taxpayer dollars support high-quality research.

The proposed rules would apply across federal agencies that award research grants. Implementation would require agencies to develop screening criteria and train political staff to review applications for prohibited subject matter.

The changes come as research institutions manage existing grant portfolios worth billions of dollars. Universities and research centers structure their budgets around expected grant funding, hiring personnel and purchasing equipment based on multi-year award commitments.

No timeline for implementing the proposed rules has been announced. The rules would need to go through a formal rulemaking process before taking effect.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: SpaceX secured major government contracts ahead of its initial public offering.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: Multiple tech companies posted coordinated messages hinting at a major laptop processor announcement.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have launched a coordinated teaser campaign for Nvidia's upcoming N1X laptop processors. Both the Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, with Arm following suit. The announcement is expected at Computex this weekend.

Microsoft's Surface chief Pavan Davuluri also teased new hardware for developers, sharing an image of what appears to be a curved display edge. The synchronized messaging from all three companies signals a significant development in Windows-based Arm laptop computing.

cards.headline: Botnet controlling 17 million devices taken down
cards.teaser: Law enforcement dismantled a massive network of compromised devices.
cards.body:
A botnet consisting of more than 17 million compromised devices has been dismantled by authorities. The network of infected computers and internet-connected devices represented one of the larger botnets disrupted in recent years.

The botnet was reportedly connected to a Russia-based residential proxy network. Such networks route internet traffic through compromised home and business devices, often without the owners' knowledge. The takedown removes a significant piece of infrastructure used for various online activities including masking the origin of internet traffic.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak sends one in five cases to hospital
cards.teaser: Analysis of a recent outbreak shows the virus caused complications in most hospitalized patients.
cards.body:
About 20 percent of measles cases in a Texas outbreak required hospitalization, according to new analysis. Most of the hospitalized patients developed complications from the virus.

The outbreak data illustrates measles infection severity in unvaccinated populations. Measles remains a highly contagious virus that spreads through the air when infected people cough or sneeze. The hospitalization rate observed in Texas aligns with known measles complication rates, which can include pneumonia, brain inflammation, and other serious conditions requiring medical treatment.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to transfer Ebola-exposed Americans
cards.teaser: A court ruling prevents the Trump administration from sending exposed individuals to Kenya.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to build a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The White House had confirmed it was setting up the facility as an alternative to bringing exposed individuals back to the United States.

Some experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could harm treatment efforts. The US has existing specialized facilities designed specifically to handle Ebola exposure cases on American soil.

cards.headline: ULA launches 29 Amazon satellites on Atlas 5 rocket
cards.teaser: United Launch Alliance successfully deployed satellites for Amazon's internet constellation.
cards.body:
United Launch Alliance successfully launched 29 Amazon satellites aboard an Atlas 5 rocket from Cape Canaveral. The mission deployed the satellites into orbit as part of Amazon's expanding Leo internet constellation project.

The launch marked the second successful flight of a busy day in Florida, following a Blue Origin mishap earlier that morning. ULA's Atlas 5 continues its role as a reliable launch vehicle for deploying commercial and government satellites.

hero.headline: Washington Nationals fire executive over hidden-camera video comments
hero.body:
The Washington Nationals fired a team official after a hidden-camera video showed him making comments about the team's social media practices regarding conservative players. The executive appeared to say the organization avoided using a Catholic pitcher on social media.

Sources told The New York Times the executive was let go after the video surfaced. The footage reportedly shows him discussing the team's approach to featuring certain players on its social platforms based on their beliefs.

Fox News reported the team faces a potential Department of Justice probe over allegations of religious discrimination. EWTN News identified the player in question as a Catholic pitcher, though the team has not publicly confirmed specific details about which players were discussed in the video.

The firing comes amid heightened scrutiny of how professional sports organizations handle employee speech and religious expression. The Nationals have not released an official statement detailing the reasons for the termination or addressing the specific allegations made in the video.

The circumstances surrounding how the video was obtained remain unclear. Hidden-camera recordings have become an increasingly common tool in modern investigative reporting, though they raise questions about journalistic methods and privacy.

The potential DOJ investigation would examine whether the team's practices violated federal laws protecting employees and contractors from religious discrimination. Such probes can take months or years to complete and may or may not result in formal charges.

The incident adds to ongoing national debates about the intersection of sports, politics, and religion. Professional teams have faced criticism from various sides for how they navigate employee expression on social and political issues.

The Nationals, based in Washington DC, play in Major League Baseball's National League East division. The team has not announced who will assume the fired executive's responsibilities or whether it plans to review its social media policies in light of the incident.

cards.headline: Pentagon recruits troops for White House UFC fights
cards.teaser: The Defense Department is recruiting military personnel to attend UFC events at the White House, according to internal memos.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is using internal memos to recruit troops for UFC fights being held at the White House, according to documents obtained by The Washington Post. CNN reported that troops must meet weight standards to receive free tickets to the events.

NBC News reported that attendees must meet specific fitness criteria to qualify for the White House UFC event. Yahoo Sports covered fighter Sean O'Malley's comments about adapting to outdoor weather conditions at the venue. Time Magazine published a profile examining how UFC president Dana White expanded the organization from niche audiences to White House events.

cards.headline: Teenager Joao Fonseca upsets Novak Djokovic at French Open
cards.teaser: Brazilian teenager Joao Fonseca defeated Novak Djokovic in the third round of the French Open, ensuring a new Grand Slam winner this year.
cards.body:
João Fonseca, a 19-year-old Brazilian player, mounted a stunning comeback to defeat Novak Djokovic 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a five-set epic at Roland Garros. After Djokovic claimed the first two sets on Court Philippe-Chatrier, the teenage prodigy battled back to claim victory in the third-round match that stretched over four hours.

The upset eliminates the 39-year-old Djokovic from contention for his 25th Grand Slam title and guarantees a new men's champion will be crowned at the tournament. The result underscores Fonseca's emergence as a legitimate title contender at the top of professional tennis.

cards.headline: Giants players Abdul Carter and Jaxson Dart address Trump rally disagreement
cards.teaser: New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter called out teammate Jaxson Dart over the quarterback's appearance at a Donald Trump rally.
cards.body:
Giants linebacker Abdul Carter publicly opposed quarterback Jaxson Dart's decision to introduce President Donald Trump at a political rally, telling the Associated Press he felt compelled to make his stance clear.

Following their disagreement, the two players found common ground. ESPN reported they later expressed unity on the matter. Giants quarterback Jameis Winston noted that difficult moments can help bring people together, while coach John Harbaugh was unlikely to criticize Dart's appearance at the event.

cards.headline: NCAA baseball tournament regionals begin
cards.teaser: The 2026 NCAA baseball tournament opened with regional play as teams compete for spots in the College World Series.
cards.body:
The NCAA baseball tournament regionals started with matchups across the country. NCAA.com published the bracket and schedule for the Men's College World Series, while ESPN offered previews of top players and predictions for the regional rounds.

Yahoo Sports examined storylines including whether UCLA can advance deep into the tournament and if the SEC will claim another title. D1Baseball released staff predictions for the regional games. USA Today provided information on game times, scores, and viewing options for the opening rounds of competition.

cards.headline: Milwaukee upsets No. 4 Auburn in NCAA baseball tournament opener
cards.teaser: Milwaukee defeated fourth-ranked Auburn in the opening round of the NCAA baseball tournament.
cards.body:
Milwaukee pulled off an upset victory over No. 4 Auburn in the teams' NCAA Tournament opener. WISN reported the result as a shock outcome, while 247Sports described the loss as an early disaster for the Tigers in what they called a lethargic performance.

Auburn coach Pat Murphy told Yahoo Sports he was happy for Milwaukee following the upset. ESPN provided video highlights of the game. The loss ended Auburn's tournament run before reaching the later rounds of regional play.

cards.headline: Sacramento launches bid for MLB expansion team
cards.teaser: An investment group in Sacramento has begun efforts to bring a Major League Baseball expansion franchise to the California city.
cards.body:
Sacramento has entered the competition for potential MLB expansion, with an investor group launching a formal bid. KCRA reported that fans in the city say they are ready for a team, while the Sacramento Bee noted some big names have already joined and departed the investment effort.

Deseret News reported Sacramento is another western city seeking an expansion franchise. The Athletic and The New York Times covered the group's announcement as part of broader MLB expansion discussions. MLB Trade Rumors compiled the Sacramento developments alongside stadium notes from Vancouver and Tampa in its expansion coverage.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who shaped Star Wars and several influential films of the 1970s, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

The family's attorney confirmed she died of cancer.

Lucas won an Academy Award for editing Star Wars, directed by her former husband George Lucas. Her work on the 1977 film helped establish the storytelling rhythm and pacing that made the science fiction epic a cultural phenomenon.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited American Graffiti and contributed to other films that defined American cinema in the 1970s. Her editing choices in Star Wars, particularly in structuring the film's climactic battle sequence and character-driven moments, proved essential to the movie's success.

Lucas was married to George Lucas during the period when he created Star Wars. The couple later divorced.

"Marcia will be remembered as a brilliant storyteller, a trailblazer," the family said in a statement released through their attorney.

Her editing career flourished during a transformative era in Hollywood filmmaking. She worked alongside directors who pioneered the New Hollywood movement, bringing a distinctive approach to film editing that emphasized emotional resonance and narrative clarity.

Lucas's death removes one of the last direct creative links to the original Star Wars production. Her contributions to the film have been increasingly recognized in recent years by film historians and critics who have examined the collaborative process behind the movie's creation.

The film editor's work extended beyond the Star Wars franchise. Her collaboration on American Graffiti helped establish George Lucas as a major director before he embarked on the space opera that would define his career.

Lucas died in Rancho Mirage, a desert city in Riverside County, California, known as a retirement community for entertainment industry professionals.

cards.headline: Over Half of Performers Drop Out of Trump-Backed Great American State Fair
cards.teaser: More than half the scheduled performers have withdrawn from a Trump-backed concert series planned for America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Artists have canceled appearances at the Great American State Fair, part of the Trump-linked Freedom 250 concert series marking the nation's 250th birthday. Martina McBride and Morris Day are among those who have pulled out of the events.

The withdrawals follow what organizers described as political pressure and threats. The concert series is connected to Freedom 250, one of two competing efforts to celebrate America's semiquincentennial, the other being America250.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Rest of 2026 Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling his remaining concert dates this year due to health issues.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling the remainder of his 2026 concert dates to focus on his health. The 92-year-old singer apologized to fans who had already purchased tickets for the shows.

Despite his age, Valli has maintained an active touring schedule throughout his decades-long career.

cards.headline: Erika Kirk Denies Dating Rumors Less Than a Year After Charlie Kirk's Death
cards.teaser: Erika Kirk responded to rumors that she has a new boyfriend following the death of her husband Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
Erika Kirk addressed claims circulating that she has moved on to a new relationship. She denied having a boyfriend and said her late husband Charlie's love will last her a lifetime.

The rumors prompted reactions from conservative commentator Matt Walsh, who criticized the speculation. Businessman Blake Wynn also broke his silence on the matter. Charlie Kirk died less than a year ago.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Film Earns Over $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The horror film from 20-year-old director Kane Parsons has already grossed more than $10 million before its nationwide theatrical release.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the directorial debut of 20-year-old Kane Parsons, has already surpassed $10 million in preview screenings. The A24 film is now in wide theatrical release.

The horror feature stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Avan Jogia, Finn Bennett, and Lukita Maxwell. The film adapts a YouTube series that inspired Parsons to develop the feature-length version.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Calls for Uncapped Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman urged gubernatorial candidates to support unlimited tax incentives for film and television production.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman appeared outside Radford Studios on Friday to advocate for uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production. She was joined by entertainment industry figures including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon, who support her mayoral campaign.

Raman called on candidates in Tuesday's gubernatorial election to back the proposal. She said the tax incentives are necessary to ensure Hollywood remains in California.

cards.headline: Kanye West Approved to Perform in Netherlands
cards.teaser: Officials cleared the rapper to enter the country for a performance on his birthday.
cards.body:
Dutch officials ruled that Kanye West can perform in the Netherlands. The decision came after a review found insufficient evidence to ban the rapper from entering the country.

The performance is scheduled to take place on West's birthday. Officials did not specify what concerns had prompted the initial review of his entry into the Netherlands.

hero.headline: Judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center, halts renovation closure
hero.body:
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. ruled that President Trump's name must be removed from the Kennedy Center and ordered a halt to the planned closure of the performing arts venue.

The decision, issued in a 94-page ruling, requires Trump to remove his name from the building and surrounding signage within two weeks. The judge wrote that it was crystal clear the arts complex was named for the late President John F. Kennedy.

The ruling also blocked the Kennedy Center from closing later this year to begin renovations. The facility had been scheduled to wind down its programming and shut down for two years of renovation work.

The judge determined that the Kennedy Center's board exceeded its legal authority by unilaterally deciding to add Trump's name to the venue. The decision represents a setback to Trump's effort to renovate the facility, which serves as the nation's cultural center and memorial to Kennedy.

The Kennedy Center, located along the Potomac River in Washington, has operated as a living memorial to President Kennedy since its opening in 1971. The ruling indicates the judge found the board lacked statutory power to rename or rebrand the facility in a way that departed from its original dedication.

Trump has not yet commented publicly on the ruling. The White House and Kennedy Center officials have not issued statements regarding compliance with the order or potential appeals.

The two-week deadline to remove Trump's name from the building will require swift action if the administration chooses to comply with the court order. The ruling leaves unclear whether the renovation plans will proceed under different terms or face further legal challenges.

The decision comes as Trump has pursued various efforts to associate his name with federal buildings and institutions during his administration. The Kennedy Center case now joins other legal disputes over presidential authority and the use of federal properties.

cards.headline: Pentagon awards Dell $9.7 billion contract amid Trump conflict concerns
cards.teaser: The Defense Department signed a five-year deal with Dell after President Trump promoted the company's products and bought its stock.
cards.body:
The Pentagon announced a $9.7 billion, five-year contract with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services to consolidate its technology infrastructure.

The deal has raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest. President Trump previously touted Dell products and purchased significant amounts of the company's stock before the contract was awarded, prompting questions about whether his financial interest influenced the procurement decision.

cards.headline: Judge reopens Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit after settlement challenge
cards.teaser: A Florida federal judge sided with intervenors who said a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund tainted the case.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The decision came after intervening parties challenged a settlement agreement between the Justice Department and Trump.

The two sides had agreed to voluntarily dismiss the suit in exchange for establishing an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge sided with the intervenors, finding that this settlement arrangement compromised the case's integrity and warranted renewed examination of the underlying claims.

cards.headline: New Jersey detention facility becomes test for new DHS Secretary Mullin
cards.teaser: Protesters have been arrested outside Delaney Hall while detainees reportedly participate in a hunger strike over conditions.
cards.body:
A private detention center in New Jersey has emerged as the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. The Delaney Hall Facility in Newark has become a flashpoint in disputes over the Trump administration's immigration policies.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced that state police will take over policing functions from federal immigration officers at the site. As part of this transition, state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators. The announcement comes as reports indicate an influx of federal agents heading to the facility, where detainees have participated in hunger strikes over claims of inhumane conditions and inadequate medical care.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Evette over Rep. Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette in a GOP primary challenge to Representative Nancy Mace.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lieutenant Governor Pam Evette in South Carolina's Republican gubernatorial primary on Friday, backing her over Representative Nancy Mace's campaign for governor. Trump announced his support in a Truth Social post, calling Evette an "America First Patriot" and describing her as a good friend, fighter, and winner.

The endorsement sets up a contested GOP primary between the sitting lieutenant governor and the congresswoman seeking the state's top office.

cards.headline: Bessent supports placing Trump on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: The Treasury Secretary endorsed the idea during an interview at the Reagan Presidential Library.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency. Bessent said the Treasury has already begun preparing for the possibility of the new currency.

Democrats have vowed to block the move. Bessent made the announcement during a news conference at the White House.

cards.headline: Democrat Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas governor poll
cards.teaser: State Representative James Talarico held 47 percent support to Attorney General Ken Paxton's 44 percent among likely voters.
cards.body:
State Representative James Talarico holds a narrow lead over Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Texas gubernatorial race, according to a poll released by Texas Public Opinion Research. The Democratic candidate received 47 percent support compared to 44 percent for his Republican opponent.

The poll surveyed likely general election voters in Texas following the primary runoff elections. The three-point margin shows a competitive race between Talarico and Paxton as both candidates prepare for the general election campaign.
